text:
Jake Neighbours tied a Blues franchise record with five assists against New Jersey on November 21, and the run hasn't stopped: 12 points in his last ten games, 11 of them assists, with three more helpers in Friday's win over Dallas. He's at 21 points in 26 games after 36 all of last season.

Enjoy it, but don't bank it. Our numbers expected about 6.5 points from those ten games at his ice time. The chances around him are ordinary (9.0 on-ice expected goals against his usual 9.5), and the Blues have scored 15.8 more goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice. That kind of on-ice luck fades. At five on five, St. Louis gets 47.9% of the expected goals with him out there.

The player underneath is still useful. Evolving-Hockey had him 34th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season, with good defensive numbers, though it also flagged that his results ran ahead of his chances. He's a 77-hit, net-front forward who gets fed good passes. His points will come back toward the middle; his role shouldn't.
